value.outcome: over 100,000 surrendered and removed to Songmo

sourceDate.text: 聖宗嘗過七金山土河之濱

place.en: forty li south of Jian Prefecture
forty li south of Jian Prefecture

units.en: Geography Treatise III — Zhongjing Circuit
units.literal: Geography Treatise III: Zhongjing Circuit

units.zh: 中京大定府，虞為營州，夏屬冀州，周在幽州之分。
units.en: Dading Prefecture at Zhongjing had been Ying Prefecture under Yu, Ji territory under Xia, and part of You under Zhou.
units.literal: Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture—in Yu's time it was Ying Prefecture; in Xia it belonged to Ji; in Zhou it lay within You's division.

units.en: When Qin organized the empire into commanderies, the region became Liaoxi.
units.literal: Qin divided the realm into commanderies; this was Liaoxi.

units.en: In Han times it was Xin'anping County.
units.literal: Under Han it was Xin'anping County.

units.zh: 漢末步奚居之，幅員千里，多大山深谷，阻險足以自固。
units.en: In late Han the Bu Xi occupied the land, a thousand-li tract of high mountains and deep valleys whose passes let them stand on their own.
units.literal: At the end of Han the Bu Xi dwelt here; the domain ran a thousand li, with many great mountains and deep valleys—defiles enough to hold themselves secure.

units.zh: 魏武北征，縱兵大戰，降者一十餘萬，去之松漠。
units.en: On his northern campaign Cao Cao fought a major engagement; over one hundred thousand men surrendered and were removed to Songmo.
units.literal: Wei Wu-di on his northern campaign loosed troops in great battle; more than a hundred thousand surrendered and were sent away to Songmo.

units.zh: 其後拓拔氏乘遼建牙於此，當饒樂河水之南，溫渝河水之北。
units.en: Later the Tuoba, exploiting turmoil in Liaodong, pitched their headquarters here between the Raole and Wenyu rivers.
units.literal: Later the Tuoba clan, seizing the moment in Liaodong, set their headquarters here—south of the Raole River, north of the Wenyu River.

units.zh: 唐太宗伐高麗，駐蹕於此。
units.en: Tang Taizong campaigned against Goryeo and encamped here on imperial progress.
units.literal: Tang Taizong campaigning against Goryeo halted his imperial progress here.

units.zh: 部帥蘇支從征有功，奚長可度率眾內附，為置饒樂都督府。
units.en: Division chief Su Zhi distinguished himself on the campaign; Xi leader Kedou brought his people to submit, and the court established Raole Protectorate.
units.literal: Division chief Su Zhi followed the campaign with merit; Xi chief Kedou led the masses to submit inward, and the Raole Protectorate was set up for them.

units.zh: 咸通以後，契丹始大，奚族不敢復抗。
units.en: After the Xiantong era the Khitan rose in power and the Xi ceased to resist.
units.literal: After Xiantong the Khitan grew great and the Xi no longer dared resist.

units.en: When Taizu founded the dynasty, the entire tribe submitted.
units.literal: When the Founder established the state, the whole tribe became subjects.

units.zh: 聖宗嘗過七金山土河之濱，南望雲氣，有郛郭樓闕之狀，因議建都。
units.en: Shengzong once traveled the Tu River below Qijin Mountain; seeing southern mists shaped like walls and gate-towers, he debated building a capital.
units.literal: Shengzong once passed the bank of Qijin Mountain and the Tu River; gazing south at cloud vapors shaped like outer walls and towered gates, he discussed founding a capital.

units.zh: 擇良工於燕、薊，董役二歲，郛郭、宮掖、樓閣、府庫、市肆廊廡，擬神都之制。
units.en: Craftsmen from Yan and Ji were recruited; for two years they built walls, palaces, towers, storehouses, and market arcades on the model of Luoyang.
units.literal: Skilled craftsmen were chosen from Yan and Ji; construction was supervised two years—outer walls, palace quarters, towers, treasuries, markets and colonnades modeled on the Divine Capital's plan.

units.zh: 統和二十四年，五帳院進故奚王牙帳地。
units.en: Tonghe year 24 brought the Five Accounts Division's gift of the old Xi royal encampment grounds.
units.literal: In Tonghe year 24 the Five Accounts Division presented the former Xi king's headquarters land.

units.zh: 二十五年，城之，實以漢戶，號曰中京，府曰大定。
units.en: In year 25 the walls rose and Han households settled it; the capital was named Zhongjing and the prefecture Dading.
units.literal: Year 25 the city was walled and filled with Han households; it was styled Zhongjing, the prefecture called Dading.

units.zh: 皇城中有祖廟，景宗、承天皇后御容殿。
units.en: The Imperial City held ancestral shrines and portrait halls for Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.
units.literal: Within the Imperial City were ancestral temples and portrait halls to Emperor Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.

units.zh: 城池湫濕，多鑿井泄之，人以不便。
units.en: The walled city sat in wet ground; numerous drainage wells were sunk, to the residents' inconvenience.
units.literal: The city moat was damp and low; many wells were dug to drain it—people found this inconvenient.

units.zh: 大同驛以待宋使，朝天館待新羅使，來賓館待夏使。
units.en: The Datong hostel lodged Song missions, Chaotian Hall Silla missions, and Laibin Hall Xia missions.
units.literal: Datong Hostel received Song envoys; Chaotian Hall received Silla envoys; Laibin Hall received Xia envoys.

units.zh: 有七金山、馬盂山、雙山、松山、土河。
units.en: Landmarks included Qijin, Mayu, Twin, and Song mountains and the Tu River.
units.literal: There were Qijin Mountain, Mayu Mountain, Twin Mountain, Song Mountain, and the Tu River.

units.en: It governed ten prefectures and nine counties:
units.literal: Ten prefectures, nine counties:

units.en: Dading County.
units.literal: Dading County.

units.en: Ancient Bai Xi land.
units.literal: Former Bai Xi territory.

units.en: Captives from many states were settled there.
units.literal: Captive households from various states were settled here.

units.en: Changxing County.
units.literal: Changxing County.

units.en: Formerly Han Bincong County.
units.literal: Originally Han Bincong County.

units.en: Various tribal communities were placed there.
units.literal: Various tribal peoples were settled here.

units.en: Fushu County.
units.literal: Fushu County.

units.zh: 本漢新安平地，開泰二年析京民置。
units.en: It was Han Xin'anping land; Kaitai year 2 carved out capital residents to found the county.
units.literal: Originally Han Xin'anping territory; in Kaitai year 2 capital households were split off to establish it.

units.en: Quannong County.
units.literal: Quannong County.

units.en: Formerly Han Bincong County ground.
units.literal: Originally Han Bincong County territory.

units.en: Kaitai year 2 detached capital households to create it.
units.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.

units.en: Wending County.
units.literal: Wending County.

units.en: Established in Kaitai year 2 from capital households.
units.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.

units.en: Shengping County.
units.literal: Shengping County.

units.en: Founded in Kaitai year 2 from capital residents.
units.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.

units.en: Guihua County.
units.literal: Guihua County.

units.en: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.

units.en: Shenshui County.
units.literal: Shenshui County.

units.en: Formerly Han Tuhe County ground.
units.literal: Originally Han Tuhe County territory.

units.en: Created in Kaitai year 2.
units.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2.

units.en: Jinyuan County.
units.literal: Jinyuan County.

units.en: Formerly within Tang Qingshan County.
units.literal: Originally Tang Qingshan County territory.

units.en: Kaitai year 2 settled it with households drawn from the capital.
units.literal: Kaitai year 2 split capital households to establish it.

units.en: En Prefecture—Huaide Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: En Prefecture, Huaide Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Han Xin'anping County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Xin'anping County territory.

units.en: Taizong created the prefecture.
units.literal: Taizong established the prefecture.

units.en: During Kaitai Bohai households were settled there.
units.literal: In Kaitai times Bohai households filled it.

units.en: It first answered to Yongxing Palace, then to Zhongjing.
units.literal: First subordinate to Yongxing Palace, later to Zhongjing.

units.en: One county: Enhua County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Enhua County.

units.en: Settled in Kaitai with Bohai households.
units.literal: Established in Kaitai from Bohai households.

units.en: Hui Prefecture—Huihe Army, middle grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Hui Prefecture, Huihe Army, middle grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Tang Guiyi Prefecture land.
units.literal: Originally Tang Guiyi Prefecture territory.

units.zh: 太祖俘漢民數百戶兔鹿山下，創城居之，置州。
units.en: Taizu took several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, built a town, and established the prefecture.
units.literal: Taizu captured several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, founded a walled settlement, and set up the prefecture.

units.en: Under Zhongjing; one county, Huihe County.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing; governing one county: Huihe County.

units.zh: 聖宗遷上京惠州民，括諸宮院落帳戶置。
units.en: Shengzong relocated Hui households from Shangjing and enrolled palace and camp registers to populate it.
units.literal: Shengzong moved Hui Prefecture households from Shangjing and gathered palace and camp registered households to settle them.

units.en: Gao Prefecture (observation commissioner).
units.literal: Gao Prefecture, observation commissioner.

units.en: Former Tang Xin Prefecture land.
units.literal: Tang Xin Prefecture territory.

units.zh: 萬歲通天元年，以契丹室活部置。
units.en: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian placed the Khitan Shihuo division here.
units.literal: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian it was set up for the Khitan Shihuo division.

units.zh: 開泰中，聖宗伐高麗，以俘戶置高州。
units.en: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo campaign founded Gao Prefecture with war captives.
units.literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and established Gao Prefecture with captives.

units.en: It has Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.
units.literal: There are Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: One county:
units.literal: Governing one county:

units.zh: 三韓縣，辰韓為扶餘，弁韓為新羅，馬韓為高麗。
units.en: Sanhan County: Chenhan stood for Fuyu, Bianhan for Silla, Mahan for Goryeo.
units.literal: Sanhan County—Chenhan was Fuyu, Bianhan Silla, Mahan Goryeo.

units.zh: 開泰中，聖宗伐高麗，俘三國之遺人置縣。
units.en: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo war placed survivors of the three Han states in the county.
units.literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and settled remnant people of the three states in the county.

units.en: 5,000 households.
units.literal: Households 5,000.

units.en: Wu'an Prefecture (observation commissioner).
units.literal: Wu'an Prefecture, observation commissioner.

units.en: Former Tang Wo Prefecture land.
units.literal: Tang Wo Prefecture territory.

units.zh: 太祖俘漢民居木葉山下，因建城以遷之，號杏堝新城。
units.en: Taizu placed Han captives below Muye Mountain, walled a new town called Apricot Ridge, and moved them in.
units.literal: Taizu settled captured Han households below Muye Mountain, built a city to move them, styled Apricot Ridge New City.

units.zh: 復以遼西戶益之，更曰新州。
units.en: Liaoxi households swelled it and the seat was renamed Xin Prefecture.
units.literal: Liaoxi households were added; it was renamed Xin Prefecture.

units.en: Tonghe year 8 gave it the present name.
units.literal: Tonghe year 8 received the present name.

units.en: It began with a prefect and was later promoted.
units.literal: At first a cishi; later promoted.

units.zh: 有黃柏嶺、裊羅水、個沒裏水。
units.en: Features include Huangbai Ridge, Liaoluo River, and Gemo River.
units.literal: There are Huangbai Ridge, Liaoluo River, and Gemo River.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: One county:
units.literal: Governing one county:

units.en: Woye County.
units.literal: Woye County.

units.en: Li Prefecture—middle grade, observation commissioner.
units.literal: Li Prefecture, middle grade, observation commissioner.

units.en: Formerly Zhongjing's Fusu County.
units.literal: Originally Zhongjing Fusu County.

units.zh: 統和二十六年置刺史州，開泰元年升。
units.en: Tonghe year 26 made it a prefecture with a cishi; in the first year of Kaitai elevated it.
units.literal: Tonghe year 26 set up as a cishi prefecture; in the first year of Kaitai promoted.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: One county:
units.literal: Governing one county:

units.en: Fusu County.
units.literal: Fusu County.

units.zh: 唐末，契丹漸熾，役使奚人，遷居琵琶川。
units.en: Late Tang saw the Khitan wax powerful, conscript Xi labor, and resettle them on the Pipa River.
units.literal: At the end of Tang the Khitan grew strong, put the Xi to labor, and moved them to dwell on the Pipa River.

units.en: Made a county in Tonghe year 4.
units.literal: Established as a county in Tonghe year 4.

units.en: It first belonged to Zhangmin Palace, then to Zhongjing.
units.literal: First subordinate to Zhangmin Palace, then reassigned to Zhongjing.

units.en: A prefecture followed, still under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Later a prefecture was set up, still subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: Yu Prefecture—Gaoping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Yu Prefecture, Gaoping Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Han Linyu County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Linyu County territory.

units.en: Later it fell under Youbeiping's Licheng County.
units.literal: Later subordinate to Youbeiping Licheng County.

units.zh: 唐載初二年，析慎州置黎州，處靺鞨部落，後為奚人所據。
units.en: In Tang Zai Chu year 2 Li Prefecture was carved from Shen to settle Mohe tribes, until the Xi took it.
units.literal: Tang Zai Chu year 2 split Shen Prefecture to set up Li Prefecture for Mohe tribes; later the Xi seized it.

units.zh: 太宗南征，橫帳解裏以所俘鎮州民置州，開泰中沒入。
units.en: On his southern campaign Taizong's Horizontal Account Jieli placed Zhen captives here; Kaitai absorbed and abolished the prefecture.
units.literal: Taizong on the southern campaign: the Horizontal Account Jieli settled captured Zhen Prefecture households and founded the prefecture; in Kaitai it was absorbed and abolished.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: Two counties:
units.literal: Governing two counties:

units.en: Hezhong County.
units.literal: Hezhong County.

units.en: Formerly Xinli County land.
units.literal: Originally Xinli County territory.

units.en: Yonghe County.
units.literal: Yonghe County.

units.en: Formerly Han Changcheng County ground.
units.literal: Originally Han Changcheng County territory.

units.en: Founded in Tonghe year 22.
units.literal: Established in Tonghe year 22.

units.en: Ze Prefecture—Guangji Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Ze Prefecture, Guangji Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Han Tuyin County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Tuyin County territory.

units.zh: 太祖俘蔚州民，立寨居之，采煉陷河銀冶。
units.en: Taizu took Wei Prefecture captives, founded a stockade, and worked the Xianhe silver mines.
units.literal: Taizu captured Wei Prefecture households, set up a stockade, and mined and smelted Xianhe silver works.

units.en: It answered to the Zhongjing regent.
units.literal: Subordinate to the Zhongjing regent's office.

units.en: Kaitai established Ze Prefecture.
units.literal: Ze Prefecture was set up in Kaitai.

units.zh: 有松亭關、神山、九宮嶺、石子嶺、濼河、撒河。
units.en: Landmarks include Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong and Shizi ridges, the Luo River, and the Sa River.
units.literal: There are Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong Ridge, Shizi Ridge, the Luo River, and the Sa River.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: Two counties:
units.literal: Governing two counties:

units.en: Shenshan County.
units.literal: Shenshan County.

units.en: Spirit Mountain stands in the southwest.
units.literal: Spirit Mountain lies to the southwest.

units.en: Luanhe County.
units.literal: Luanhe County.

units.en: Formerly Han Xuwu County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Xuwu County territory.

units.en: Under Yongxing Palace.
units.literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.

units.en: Bei'an Prefecture—Xinghua Army, upper grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Bei'an Prefecture, Xinghua Army, upper grade, cishi.

units.zh: 本漢女祁縣地，屬上谷郡。
units.en: Formerly Han Nuqi County in Shanggu Commandery.
units.literal: Originally Han Nuqi County territory, belonging to Shanggu Commandery.

units.en: Jin times saw Feng Ba take it.
units.literal: Under Jin it was seized by Feng Ba.

units.en: Tang made it the Xi princely house's western domain.
units.literal: Under Tang it was western territory of the Xi princely mansion.

units.en: Shengzong placed Han households and founded Bei'an Prefecture.
units.literal: Shengzong settled Han households to establish Bei'an Prefecture.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: One county: Xinghua County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Xinghua County.

units.en: Formerly Han Qieju County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Qieju County territory.

units.en: Tan Prefecture—Guangrun Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Tan Prefecture, Guangrun Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.zh: 本中京之龍山縣，開泰中置州，仍屬中京。
units.en: It was Zhongjing's Longshan County; Kaitai made it a prefecture still under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Originally Longshan County of Zhongjing; the prefecture was set up in Kaitai and remained under Zhongjing.

units.en: One county: Longshan County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Longshan County.

units.en: Formerly Han Jiaoli County ground.
units.literal: Originally Han Jiaoli County territory.

units.en: Kaitai year 2 founded it from Xijia Stockade.
units.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Xijia Stockade.

units.en: Songshan Prefecture—Sheng'an territory, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Songshan Prefecture, Sheng'an territory, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Created in Kaitai.
units.literal: Established in Kaitai.

units.en: Tonghe year 8 abolished it; later it was restored.
units.literal: Abolished in Tonghe year 8, then restored.

units.en: Under Zhongjing.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: One county:
units.literal: Governing one county:

units.en: Songshan County.
units.literal: Songshan County.

units.en: Formerly Han Wencheng County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Wencheng County territory.

units.en: On the Songmo frontier, a hub of trade.
units.literal: Bordering Songmo, a merchant crossroads.

units.en: Made a county in Kaitai year 2.
units.literal: Established as a county in Kaitai year 2.

units.en: The Song Mountain river runs through it.
units.literal: There is the Song Mountain stream.

units.zh: 宋王曾《上契丹事》曰：出燕京北門，至望京館。
units.en: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: from Yanjing's north gate to Wangjing Hostel,
units.literal: Song minister Wang Zeng's Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan says: leaving Yanjing's north gate, one reaches Wangjing Hostel.

units.en: fifty li to Shun Prefecture;
units.literal: fifty li to Shun Prefecture.

units.en: seventy li to Tan Prefecture as the road climbs into hills;
units.literal: seventy li to Tan Prefecture, gradually entering mountains.

units.en: another fifty li reaches Jingou Hostel.
units.literal: fifty li to Jingou Hostel.

units.zh: 將至館，川原平曠，謂之金溝澱。
units.en: Near the hostel the valley floor widens into what they call the Jingou flats.
units.literal: Approaching the hostel, the river plain opens wide—called the Jingou shoals.

units.zh: 自此入山，詰曲登陟，無復裏堠，但以馬行記日，約其里數。
units.en: Beyond lies twisting mountain grades without mileposts; travelers count days on horseback to reckon distance.
units.literal: From here one enters the mountains, winding up steep paths; there are no more mile markers—only days on horseback estimate the distance.

units.zh: 九十里至古北口，兩傍峻崖，僅容車軌。
units.en: Ninety li brings Gubeikou, where cliffs on both sides admit only a single cart track.
units.literal: Ninety li to Gubeikou; steep cliffs on both sides barely admit a cart track.

units.zh: 又度德勝嶺，盤道數層，俗名思鄉嶺，八十里至新館。
units.en: Desheng Ridge's switchbacks, known as Homesick Ridge, lead eighty li to Xin Hostel.
units.literal: Crossing Desheng Ridge with its layered switchbacks—folk name Homesick Ridge—eighty li to Xin Hostel.

units.zh: 過雕窠嶺、偏槍嶺，四十里至臥如來館。
units.en: Past Diaoke and Pianqiang ridges, forty li to the Reclining Tathagata Hostel.
units.literal: Passing Diaoke Ridge and Pianqiang Ridge, forty li to Wolai Hostel.

units.zh: 過烏灤河，東有灤州，又過摸鬥嶺，一名渡雲嶺，芹菜嶺，七十里至柳河館。
units.en: The Wuluan River is crossed with Luan Prefecture eastward; Modou Ridge, alias Duyun and Qincai ridges, lies seventy li before Liuhe Hostel.
units.literal: Crossing the Wuluan River—with Luan Prefecture to the east—then Modou Ridge, also called Duyun Ridge and Qincai Ridge; seventy li to Liuhe Hostel.

units.zh: 松亭嶺甚險峻，七十里至打造部落館。
units.en: Songting Ridge is sheer; seventy li farther stands the Forging Tribes Hostel.
units.literal: Songting Ridge is very precipitous; seventy li to the Forging Tribes Hostel.

units.zh: 東南行五十里至牛山館。
units.en: Fifty li southeast to Niushan Hostel.
units.literal: Southeast fifty li to Niushan Hostel.

units.en: Eighty li to Deer Gorge Hostel.
units.literal: Eighty li to Lu'er Gorge Hostel.

units.zh: 過蝦蟆嶺，九十里至鐵漿館。
units.en: Over Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Iron-Slurry Hostel.
units.literal: Crossing Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Tiejiang Hostel.

units.zh: 過石子嶺，自此漸出山，七十里至富谷館。
units.en: Shizi Ridge passed, the road slowly descends from the hills; seventy li to Fugu Hostel.
units.literal: Crossing Shizi Ridge, from here gradually leaving the mountains, seventy li to Fugu Hostel.

units.zh: 八十里至通天館，二十里至中京大定府。
units.en: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, then twenty li to Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.
units.literal: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, twenty li to Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture.

units.zh: 城垣卑小，方圓才四里許。
units.en: Walls are low and the city circuit scarcely four li around.
units.literal: The walls are low and small; the circuit barely four li square.

units.en: Gatehouses are stacked roofs without barbican towers.
units.literal: Gates are only layered roofs, without tower-gate construction.

units.zh: 南門曰朱夏，門內通步廊，多坊門。
units.en: The south gate Zhuxia opens on covered walkways and many lane gates.
units.literal: The south gate is called Zhuxia; within the gate connected walking corridors and many ward gates.

units.zh: 又有市樓四：曰天方、大衢、通阛、望闕。
units.en: Four market towers stand: Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.
units.literal: There are also four market towers: called Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.

units.en: Farther on lies Datong Hostel.
units.literal: Next one reaches Datong Hostel.

units.en: Its north-facing gate bears the names Yangde and Changge.
units.literal: Its gate due north is called Yangde and Changge.

units.en: A temple crowns a southwest hill inside the walls.
units.literal: Within the city on a hillock in the southwest corner is a temple.

units.en: South of the walls lie gardens used for feasts and archery.
units.literal: South of the city are gardens, a place for banquets and archery.

units.zh: 自過古北口，居人草庵板屋，耕種，但無桑柘；
units.en: Beyond Gubeikou people dwell in thatch huts and plank houses and till fields, yet plant no mulberry or catalpa;
units.literal: From passing Gubeikou, inhabitants live in thatched huts and plank houses and farm, but there is no mulberry or catalpa;

units.zh: 所種皆從壟上，虞吹沙所壅。
units.en: crops are sown on ridge tops for fear windblown sand would bury them.
units.literal: all planting is on ridge crests, lest blown sand bury the crops.

units.zh: 山中長松郁然，深谷中時見畜牧牛馬橐駝，多青羊黃豕。
units.en: Mountains hold thick pine; valleys often show cattle, horses, and camels, with many blue sheep and yellow hogs.
units.literal: In the mountains tall pines grow dense; deep valleys sometimes show pastured cattle, horses, and camels—many blue sheep and yellow swine.

units.en: Cheng Prefecture—Xingfu Army, military commissioner.
units.literal: Cheng Prefecture, Xingfu Army, military commission.

units.zh: 晉國長公主以媵戶置，軍曰長慶，隸上京。
units.en: The Jin Senior Princess founded it with dowry households under the Changqing army, subordinate to Shangjing.
units.literal: The Jin state's Senior Princess established it with dowry households; the army was called Changqing, subordinate to Shangjing.

units.en: The army designation was later renamed.
units.literal: The army name was changed again.

units.en: One county: Tongchang County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Tongchang County.

units.en: Xingzhong Prefecture.
units.literal: Xingzhong Prefecture.

units.en: Formerly Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army), military commissioner.
units.literal: Originally Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.

units.en: Land of ancient Guzhu.
units.literal: The ancient Guzhu state.

units.en: Han Liucheng County ground.
units.literal: Han Liucheng County territory.

units.zh: 慕容皝以柳城之北，龍山之南，福德之地，乃築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣，遂遷都，號曰和龍宮。
units.en: Murong Huang deemed the tract between Liucheng and Long Mountain auspicious, built Long City with palaces and shrines, renamed Liucheng Longcheng County, moved the capital, and called it Helong Palace.
units.literal: Murong Huang, taking the land north of Liucheng and south of Long Mountain as a place of fortune and virtue, built Long City, erected palaces and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng County, moved the capital, and styled it Helong Palace.

units.zh: 慕容垂復居焉，後為北跋所滅。
units.en: Murong Chui returned there; Northern Yan later destroyed it.
units.literal: Murong Chui dwelt there again; later it was destroyed by Northern Yan.

units.en: Northern Wei made it Liaoxi Commandery.
units.literal: Northern Wei took it as Liaoxi Commandery.

units.en: Sui subdued Gao Baoning and established Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Sui pacified Gao Baoning and set up Ying Prefecture.

units.en: Sui Yang-di abolished the prefecture for Liucheng Commandery.
units.literal: Emperor Yang abolished the prefecture and set up Liucheng Commandery.

units.zh: 唐武德初改營州總管府，尋為都督府。
units.en: Early Tang Wude made it Ying chief command, soon a protectorate seat.
units.literal: Early Tang Wude changed it to Ying Prefecture chief commandery, soon a protectorate headquarters.

units.en: Wansui Tongtian saw it lost to Li Wanrong.
units.literal: In Wansui Tongtian it fell to Li Wanrong.

units.en: Early Shenlong shifted the seat to Youzhou.
units.literal: Early Shenlong moved the headquarters to Youzhou.

units.en: Kaiyuan year 4 returned government to Liucheng.
units.literal: Kaiyuan year 4 restored administration at Liucheng.

units.en: Year 8 the seat moved west to Yuyang.
units.literal: Year 8 it moved west to Yuyang.

units.en: Year 10 brought it back to Liucheng.
units.literal: Year 10 it returned to Liucheng.

units.en: The Xi later held it.
units.literal: Later the Xi seized it.

units.zh: 太祖平奚及俘燕民，將建城，命韓知方擇其處。
units.en: Taizu subdued the Xi, took Yan captives, and charged Han Zhifang to choose a city site.
units.literal: Taizu pacified the Xi and captured Yan households; intending to build a city, he ordered Han Zhifang to choose the site.

units.zh: 乃完葺柳城，號霸州彰武軍，節度。
units.en: Liucheng was rebuilt as Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army) with a military commissioner.
units.literal: Liucheng was then repaired and styled Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.

units.zh: 統和中，制置建、霸、宜、錦、白川等五州。
units.en: Tonghe created a frontier commission over Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan prefectures.
units.literal: In Tonghe times the frontier commission of Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan five prefectures was set up.

units.en: The commission was soon dropped and the seat joined Jiqing Palace.
units.literal: Soon the commission was abolished; it was subordinate to Jiqing Palace.

units.en: Later it passed to Xingsheng Palace.
units.literal: Later it belonged to Xingsheng Palace.

units.en: Chongxi year 10 elevated it to Xingzhong Prefecture.
units.literal: Chongxi year 10 it was promoted to Xingzhong Prefecture.

units.zh: 有大華山、小華山、香高山、麝香崖，天授皇帝刻石在焉，駐龍峪、神射泉、小靈河。
units.en: It boasts Great and Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk Cliff with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's inscription, Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.
units.literal: There are Great Huashan, Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk-fragrance Cliff—with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's carved stone—Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.

units.en: It governed two prefectures and four counties:
units.literal: Two prefectures, four counties:

units.en: Xingzhong County.
units.literal: Xingzhong County.

units.en: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.

units.zh: 太祖掠漢民居此，建霸城縣。
units.en: Taizu settled plundered Han households and founded Bacheng County.
units.literal: Taizu plundered Han households to dwell here and built Bacheng County.

units.en: Chongxi established the prefecture and renamed the county.
units.literal: In Chongxi the prefecture was set up and the name changed.

units.en: Yingqiu County.
units.literal: Yingqiu County.

units.en: Carved from Bacheng.
units.literal: Split off from Bacheng.

units.en: Xianglei County.
units.literal: Xianglei County.

units.en: Kaitai year 2 founded it on the Maiwu River.
units.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Maiwu River.

units.en: First under Zhongjing.
units.literal: First subordinate to Zhongjing.

units.en: Later subordinate.
units.literal: Later subordinate.

units.en: Lüshan County.
units.literal: Lüshan County.

units.en: Formerly Han Qielü County.
units.literal: Originally Han Qielü County.

units.en: Kaitai year 2 created it from the Luo Family Army.
units.literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from the Luo Family Army.

units.en: First under Zhongjing, later under the prefecture.
units.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing, later subordinate.

units.en: An'de Prefecture—Huaping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: An'de Prefecture, Huaping Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Created from Ba's An'de County and attached here.
units.literal: Set up from Ba Prefecture's An'de County; came under this prefecture.

units.en: One county: An'de County.
units.literal: Governing one county: An'de County.

units.zh: 統和八年析霸城東南龍山徒河境戶置。
units.en: Tonghe year 8 settled households from southeast Bacheng and the Long Mountain and Tuhe marches.
units.literal: Tonghe year 8 split households from southeast Bacheng, Long Mountain, and Tuhe borders to establish it.

units.zh: 初隸乾州，更屬霸州，置州來屬。
units.en: It first belonged to Qian, then Ba; establishing the prefecture brought it here.
units.literal: First subordinate to Qian Prefecture, then to Ba Prefecture; when the prefecture was set up it came under this seat.

units.en: Qian Prefecture—Fuchang Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Qian Prefecture, Fuchang Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Han Liaoxi Commandery land.
units.literal: Originally Han Liaoxi Commandery territory.

units.zh: 太祖平渤海，以所俘戶居之，隸黑水河提轄司。
units.en: Taizu conquered Bohai, placed captives here under the Blackwater River commissioner.
units.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and settled captives here, subordinate to the Blackwater River commissioner.

units.zh: 安帝置州，析宜、霸二州漢戶益之。
units.en: Emperor An founded the prefecture and augmented it with Han households from Yi and Ba.
units.literal: Emperor An established the prefecture and added Han households split from Yi and Ba prefectures.

units.zh: 初隸永興宮，更隸中京，後置府，來屬。
units.en: It passed from Yongxing Palace to Zhongjing, then to Xingzhong when that prefecture rose.
units.literal: First subordinate to Yongxing Palace, then to Zhongjing; after the prefecture was set up it came under this seat.

units.en: One county: Shengji County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Shengji County.

units.zh: 太祖平渤海，俘興州盛吉縣民來居，因置縣。
units.en: Taizu pacified Bohai; captives from Xing Prefecture's Shengji County were settled here and the county founded.
units.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai; captives from Xing Prefecture's Shengji County were settled here and the county established.

units.en: Yi Prefecture—Chongyi Army, upper grade, military commissioner.
units.literal: Yi Prefecture, Chongyi Army, upper grade, military commission.

units.en: Formerly Liaoxi Lei County land.
units.literal: Originally Liaoxi Lei County territory.

units.en: The Dongdan king autumn-hunted here each year.
units.literal: The Dongdan king hunted here every autumn.

units.en: Xingzong founded it with Ding Prefecture captives.
units.literal: Xingzong established the prefecture with captives from Ding Prefecture.

units.zh: 有墳山，松柏連亙百餘里，禁樵采，浚河，累石為堤。
units.en: Tomb Mountain bears pines and cypress for a hundred li with logging banned; the river was dredged and stone dikes raised.
units.literal: There is Tomb Mountain; pines and cypresses run more than a hundred li; fuel cutting is forbidden; the river was dredged and stones piled for dikes.

units.en: Under Jiqing Palace.
units.literal: Subordinate to Jiqing Palace.

units.en: Two counties:
units.literal: Governing two counties:

units.en: Hongzheng County.
units.literal: Hongzheng County.

units.en: Shizong settled it with Ding captives.
units.literal: Shizong established it with Ding Prefecture captives.

units.en: Han craftsmen weave cloth with notable skill.
units.literal: Han laborers weave cloth; many are skilled.

units.en: Wenyi County.
units.literal: Wenyi County.

units.en: Shizong founded it.
units.literal: Established by Shizong.

units.en: It first belonged to Haibei Prefecture, then to Yi.
units.literal: First subordinate to Haibei Prefecture, later came under this seat.

units.en: Jin Prefecture—Linhai Army, middle grade, military commissioner.
units.literal: Jin Prefecture, Linhai Army, middle grade, military commission.

units.en: Formerly Han Liaodong Wulü County.
units.literal: Originally Han Liaodong Wulü County.

units.en: Murong Huang established Xile County.
units.literal: Murong Huang set up Xile County.

units.en: Taizu founded the prefecture with Han captives.
units.literal: Taizu established the prefecture with Han captives.

units.zh: 有大胡僧山、小胡僧山、大查牙山、小查牙山、淘河島。
units.en: Landmarks include Great and Little Huseng and Chaya mountains and Taohe Island.
units.literal: There are Great Huseng Mountain, Little Huseng Mountain, Great Chaya Mountain, Little Chaya Mountain, and Taohe Island.

units.en: Under Hongyi Palace.
units.literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace.

units.en: It governed one prefecture and two counties:
units.literal: One prefecture, two counties:

units.en: Yongle County.
units.literal: Yongle County.

units.en: Anchang County.
units.literal: Anchang County.

units.en: Yan Prefecture—Baosu Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Yan Prefecture, Baosu Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Han Haiyang County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Haiyang County territory.

units.zh: 太祖平渤海，遷漢戶雜居興州境，聖宗於此建城焉。
units.en: Taizu after conquering Bohai mingled Han households in Xing Prefecture; Shengzong walled a city here.
units.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and moved Han households to mix in Xing Prefecture territory; Shengzong built a city here.

units.en: Under Hongyi Palace, then attached to Jin Prefecture.
units.literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace; came under this prefecture.

units.en: One county: Xingcheng County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Xingcheng County.

units.en: Chuan Prefecture—Changning Army, middle grade, military commissioner.
units.literal: Chuan Prefecture, Changning Army, middle grade, military commission.

units.en: Formerly Tang Qingshan Prefecture land.
units.literal: Originally Tang Qingshan Prefecture territory.

units.en: Taizu's brother Prince Ming, Anduan, founded it.
units.literal: Taizu's younger brother Prince Ming Wang Anduan established it.

units.en: Huitong year 3 renamed it Baichuan Prefecture by edict.
units.literal: Huitong year 3 an edict styled it Baichuan Prefecture.

units.zh: 安端子察割以大逆誅，沒入，省曰川州。
units.en: Anduan's son Chalie was executed for great treason; the domain was confiscated and the seat abbreviated to Chuan Prefecture.
units.literal: Anduan's son Chalie was executed for great treason; the land was confiscated and abbreviated to Chuan Prefecture.

units.zh: 初隸崇德宮，統和中屬文忠王府。
units.en: It first answered to Chongde Palace; Tonghe placed it under the Wenzhong princely house.
units.literal: First subordinate to Chongde Palace; in Tonghe it belonged to the Wenzhong princely mansion.

units.en: Three counties:
units.literal: Governing three counties:

units.en: Hongli County.
units.literal: Hongli County.

units.zh: 統和八年以諸宮提轄司戶置。
units.en: Tonghe year 8 settled it with households from palace commissioners.
units.literal: Tonghe year 8 established it with households from various palace commissioners.

units.en: Xiankang County.
units.literal: Xiankang County.

units.en: Yimin County.
units.literal: Yimin County.

units.en: Founded in Tonghe.
units.literal: Established in Tonghe.

units.en: Jian Prefecture—Baojing Army, upper grade, military commissioner.
units.literal: Jian Prefecture, Baojing Army, upper grade, military commission.

units.en: Changle County was set up in Tang Wude.
units.literal: In Tang Wude, Changle County was established.

units.en: Taizu restored the old walls and founded the prefecture.
units.literal: Taizu completed the old ramparts and established the prefecture.

units.zh: 漢乾祐元年，故石晉太后詣世宗，求於漢城側耕墾自贍。
units.en: In Han Qianyou 1 the former Jin empress dowager visited Shizong, requesting land beside Hancheng to farm and provide for herself.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianyou of Han, the former Jin empress dowager came to Shizong, asking to farm and support herself beside Hancheng.

units.zh: 許於建州南四十里給地五十頃，營構房室，創立宗廟。
units.en: Permission was given for fifty qing of land forty li south of Jian Prefecture, with houses built and an ancestral temple founded.
units.literal: He granted fifty qing of land forty li south of Jian Prefecture, built houses, and founded an ancestral temple.

units.zh: 州在靈河之南，屢遭水害，聖宗遷於河北康崇州故城。
units.en: The seat south of Ling River suffered repeated inundation; Shengzong relocated it to the old Kangchong Prefecture city north of the river.
units.literal: The prefecture lay south of Ling River and suffered repeated floods; Shengzong moved it to the old city of Kangchong Prefecture north of the river.

units.zh: 初名武寧軍，隸永興宮，後屬敦睦宮。
units.en: It was first titled the Wuning Army, under Yongxing Palace, later attached to Dunmu Palace.
units.literal: At first named Wuning Army; subordinate to Yongxing Palace; later under Dunmu Palace.

units.en: Two counties:
units.literal: Governing two counties:

units.en: Yongba County.
units.literal: Yongba County.

units.en: Yongkang County.
units.literal: Yongkang County.

units.en: Formerly Tang Changli County land.
units.literal: Originally Tang Changli County territory.

units.en: Lai Prefecture—Guide Army, lower grade, military commissioner.
units.literal: Lai Prefecture, Guide Army, lower grade, military commission.

units.zh: 聖宗以女直五部歲饑來歸，置州居之。
units.en: Shengzong received the five Jurchen divisions in famine years and founded the prefecture to house them.
units.literal: Shengzong, when the five Jurchen divisions came in famine, settled them and set up the prefecture.

units.en: It began with a prefect and was later elevated.
units.literal: At first a cishi; later promoted.

units.en: Under Yongxing Palace.
units.literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.

units.zh: 有三州山、六州山、五脂山。
units.en: It has Sanzhou, Liuzhou, and Wuzhi mountains.
units.literal: There are Sanzhou Mountain, Liuzhou Mountain, and Wuzhi Mountain.

units.en: It governed two prefectures and one county, Laibin County.
units.literal: Two prefectures, one county: Laibin County.

units.en: Formerly Tang Laiyuan County land.
units.literal: Originally Tang Laiyuan County territory.

units.en: Xi Prefecture—Pinghai Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Xi Prefecture, Pinghai Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Murong Huang established Jining County.
units.literal: Murong Huang set up Jining County.

units.zh: 聖宗括帳戶遷信州，大雪不能進，建城於此，置焉。
units.en: Shengzong mustered registers to relocate to Xin Prefecture; snow halted the march, so a city and prefecture were founded here.
units.literal: Shengzong gathered registered households to move to Xin Prefecture; heavy snow blocked the way, so a city was built here and the prefecture set up.

units.en: Under Xingsheng Palace; then attached here.
units.literal: Subordinate to Xingsheng Palace; came under this prefecture.

units.en: One county: Haibin County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Haibin County.

units.en: Formerly a Han county.
units.literal: Originally a Han county.

units.zh: 瀕海，地多堿鹵，置鹽場於此。
units.en: It borders the sea on saline soil where salt pans were established.
units.literal: Coastal; the ground is much alkaline salt; salt works were set up here.

units.en: Qian Prefecture—Xingshan Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Qian Prefecture, Xingshan Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Formerly Han Yangle County land.
units.literal: Originally Han Yangle County territory.

units.zh: 聖宗平大延琳，遷歸州民置，來屬。
units.en: After pacifying Da Yanlin, Shengzong resettled Gui Prefecture people here and attached the seat.
units.literal: Shengzong pacified Da Yanlin and moved Gui Prefecture households here; came under this prefecture.

units.en: It has Jiangan Mountain.
units.literal: There is Jiangan Mountain.

units.en: One county: Qianmin County.
units.literal: Governing one county: Qianmin County.

units.en: Run Prefecture—Haiyang Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Run Prefecture, Haiyang Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.zh: 聖宗平大延琳，遷寧州之民居此，置州。
units.en: After Da Yanlin's defeat Shengzong relocated Ning Prefecture households and founded Run Prefecture.
units.literal: Shengzong pacified Da Yanlin and moved Ning Prefecture households here and set up the prefecture.

units.en: One county:
units.literal: Governing one county:

units.en: Haiyang County.
units.literal: Haiyang County.

units.zh: 本漢陽樂縣地，遷潤州，本東京城內渤海民戶，因叛，移於此。
units.en: Formerly Han Yangle County; Run Prefecture received Eastern Capital Bohai households moved here after a revolt.
units.literal: Originally Han Yangle County territory; moved to Run Prefecture—originally Bohai households within the Eastern Capital inner city, relocated here because of rebellion.
